rejectionReason: The workflow emits free-form security issue recommendations or no-op outputs, but neither provides a deterministic, repository-evidenced binding from an assigned finding to a verified remediation outcome.

decisions.selected: Verified remediation of a setup-action security finding
alternatives: Creation of an actionable security issue
decisions.rationale: The workflow asks for actionable issue recommendations for significant findings; issue creation and audit completion are outputs or activity, not the security outcome.

decisions.selected: A specific security finding reported for actions/setup/
alternatives: All files scanned in a run
decisions.rationale: A finding is the smallest unit for which remediation could be attained; files and aspects measure audit coverage rather than remediation.

decisions.selected: Blocked: no stable finding identifier or structured finding-to-run binding exists
alternatives: Issue title prefix and creation time
decisions.rationale: The required [setup-security] title prefix identifies a reporting channel but not a distinct finding, and historical replay must reconstruct assignments when case and event are null.

decisions.selected: Blocked: no deterministic accepted evidence proves that a reported finding was remediated
alternatives: Merged pull request mentioning the issue
decisions.rationale: Issue closure and textual references do not establish that the reported vulnerability was fixed; the workflow does not require a machine-readable finding fingerprint or remediation acceptance rule.
The adoption commit adds the workflow, while pre-adoption repository evidence has no frozen, comparable finding assignment and direct remediation contract.

uncertainties.description: A run may create up to three issues, while no structured finding ID is required in issue titles or bodies for historical reconstruction.
The workflow defines recommendation content but no repository state that deterministically verifies a finding's remediation.
The local first-adoption commit has no available parent, and existing setup-security issues cannot be scored under a direct remediation contract.
